doc.title: Bob Magnusson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Opening: working with Roger Kellaway and John Guerin
summary: Monk Rowe introduces Magnusson after a set with Roger Kellaway. Magnusson praises Kellaway's versatility and adventurous spirit and mentions their trio CD.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we are in Los Angeles filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. I’m very pleased to have Bob Magnusson with me, after a burning set at the International Jazz Party. I have a feeling when you work with Roger it’s always an adventure.
Roger Kellaway — I should tell my film audience.

Yeah I love working with Roger Kellaway and John Guerin. We’ve been trying to do something as a trio. It’s kind of hard to get anybody to — we’ve made a CD but we haven’t been able to get anybody to buy it. Roger does — he’s such a versatile musician. He’s done film writing and composed concertos for orchestras, and you name it and he’s done it. And he has this terrific spirit of adventure when he plays, like you were bringing out. And so I really have to pay attention. It can go any place at any time with Roger.
Yeah. And it does, so I have to really stay awake.
